question: A 3.5-year-old boy has a fragile skeleton with a history of repeated fractures. He has short stature, clinical evaluation reveals growth retardation, blue sclera, teeth abnormalities, and impaired hearing. His older sister also has similar complaints. His parents had consanguineous marriage. Which of the following is the best diagnosis?
Which of the following is an IL-6 receptor antagonist that is also found to be effective in treating rheumatoid arthritis?
Which of the following is a disease modifying antirheumatic drug whose active metabolite inhibits the enzyme dihydroorotate dehydrogenase?

A 1-month-old infant was presented to the outpatient department with a complaint of restricted movement of the hip. On examination, both the Ortolani and Barlow tests were positive. What is the best treatment option for this infant?

A 5-year-old child with a small face, short stature, abnormal gait and low IQ is brought to OPD for diagnosis. You suspect a complex congenital skeletal and neurological abnormality. Which of the following would be the first line imaging modality?

A 55-year-old man presents with back pain, fever, and malaise for 3 weeks. MRI of the lumbar spine shows abnormal bone marrow signals in L4-L5 vertebral bodies, and the intervening disc appears hypointense on T1-weighted images and hyperintense on T2-weighted images, showing heterogeneous post-contrast enhancement. It is associated with peripherally enhancing collection in the pre- and paravertebral region. No evidence of collection in epidural extension. The rest of the vertebrae appear unremarkable. The given explanation best corresponds to which one of the following conditions?

A 16-month-old child is brought to paediatric OPD with complaint of swelling around the wrist joint. The paediatrician clinically suspects rickets. Which of the following radiographic findings is most characteristic of rickets on x-ray wrist?
A 14-year-old boy presented with left knee pain and swelling, which is more severe at night. There is no pain. What is the role of MRI in this case?

answers.option: To assess the extent of the tumor
To identify calcification within the tumor
To assess the margin of the tumor

question: A 10-year-old boy presented with repeated fractures, anemia, hydrocephaly and cranial nerve defects. Radiograph of the upper extremity showed diffusely sclerotic bones with poorly formed distal metaphyses of the ulna and radius. This rare genetic disease is characterised by reduced bone resorption and diffuse, symmetric skeletal sclerosis due to impaired osteoclast function. The Doctor advised hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. Which one of the following diseases occurs due to a defect in the gene for the enzyme carbonic anhydrase 2 (CA2)?

A 7-year-old girl presented with a 3-week history of joint pain and swelling in her left knee and right ankle. Her mother reports that the child has been limping in the mornings, with stiffness that improves as the day progresses. There is no history of trauma or recent travel. She had a sore throat about a month ago. On examination, both joints are swollen and warm, with a limited range of motion. No skin rash or fever is noted. Which is the most appropriate next step in evaluating this patient?

answers.option: Reassure the family and observe for another 2 weeks
Start empirical antibiotics for septic arthritis
Order antistreptolysin O (ASO) titer and throat swab culture
Obtain complete blood count, ESR/CRP, ANA, and perform joint aspiration if necessary
Prescribe NSAIDs and refer to orthopedic surgery

question: A 65-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with postmenopausal osteoporosis has no history of fractures and no other pertinent medical conditions. Which is most appropriate for management of her osteoporosis?
A 65-year-old woman who has been diagnosed with postmenopausal osteoporosis was started treatment with Alendronate. Which is correct regarding the pharmacokinetics of the bisphosphonates?

answers.option: Bisphosphonate is cleared from the plasma by binding to bone.
Food or other medications greatly enhance absorption of bisphosphonates.
Elimination half-life of bisphosphonates ranges from 4 to 6 hours.
Bisphosphonates are well absorbed after oral administration.
Bisphosphonates are mainly metabolized via the cytochrome P450 system.

question: Which of the following drugs is used for the treatment of severe chronic inflammatory disorders, with special precautions to guard against the development of irreversible retinopathy?

A 44-year-old woman was found to have a plasma urate level of 13 mg/dL and 800 mg/24 hrs of uric acid in her urine during a routine checkup. She started an appropriate treatment and three weeks later her plasma urate levels were 7.2 mg/dL and the urinary uric acid level 530 mg/24 hrs. Which of the following drugs was most likely prescribed?
Which of the following NSAIDs would be the most appropriate choice for a patient with a history of peptic ulcer disease?

A 58-year-old postmenopausal woman's condition was not sufficiently controlled with alendronate, so she began therapy with a nasal spray containing a protein that inhibits bone resorption. Which drug was contained in the nasal spray?
Which of the following drugs can interfere with leukocyte microtubule polymerisation and thus exert potent anti-inflammatory effects in gout?
A 70-year-old female suffering from bone pain due to osteoporosis was prescribed Alendronate. Which one of the following is the mechanism of action of this agent?

answers.option: Enhances the activation of Vitamin D

question: A patient with which one of the following disorders is at high risk for developing hyperphosphatemia?
Uric acid is the degradation product of which of the following?

A 54-year-old man presents to the emergency department with a sudden onset of severe pain, redness, and swelling in his right big toe that began overnight. He describes the pain as excruciating and notes that even the pressure of a bedsheet is unbearable. He has a history of hypertension and consumes alcohol regularly. On examination, the right first metatarsophalangeal (MTP) joint is erythematous, swollen, and extremely tender. His temperature is 37.8°C. Joint aspiration reveals needle-shaped, negatively birefringent crystals under polarized light microscopy. What is the most likely diagnosis?
Which of the following enzymes uses phosphoribosyl pyrophosphate (PRPP) in the purine salvage pathway to convert free purine bases into nucleotide forms?

A 68-year-old postmenopausal woman presents with chronic back pain after a low-impact fall resulting in a vertebral compression fracture. She leads a sedentary lifestyle and does not take calcium or vitamin D supplements. Bone mineral density testing confirms osteoporosis. Which of the following best explains the cellular mechanism responsible for her condition?

answers.option: Osteoblast activity exceeds osteoclast activity, leading to dense but brittle bone
A failure of osteocytes to signal the need for remodeling in weight-bearing areas
Osteoclast-mediated bone resorption exceeds osteoblast-mediated bone formation
Total cessation of both osteoblast and osteoclast activity
Excessive mineralization of the osteoid matrix leading to decreased flexibility

question: A 65-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with generalized bone pain and proximal muscle weakness. Laboratory results reveal low serum calcium, low phosphate, elevated alkaline phosphatase (ALP), and very low 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels. Which of the following radiographic findings is most pathognomonic for osteomalacia?

A 34-year-old female presents to the outpatient department with lethargy, difficulty and pain in holding household objects in the morning for the past six months. She also reports low‑grade fever over the same period. Examination reveals warm, tender metacarpophalangeal and small joints of the hands with ulnar deviation. Which of the following is the most specific diagnostic test for her condition?
After spinal injury, the return of which reflex indicates the end of spinal shock?

A 35-year-old male had a history of a fall from a height, sustained a burst fracture of the L1 vertebrae. Which one of the following best describes the burst fracture according to Denis three-column theory?

answers.option: Failure of anterior and middle columns

question: A 6-year-old child falls on an outstretched hand. The elbow is swollen and deformed, and the distal pulses are weak. Which of the following is the best management plan?

A 25-year-old male athlete falls during a football game and sustains a direct blow to his upper arm. X-rays reveal a fracture of the surgical neck of the humerus with displacement. Which nerve is the most at risk for injury in this fracture?

A 10-year-old boy falls on an outstretched hand. He presents with pain in the forearm and elbow. X-ray shows a proximal third ulna fracture with anterior dislocation of the radial head. What is the most likely diagnosis?
Recurrent shoulder dislocation most commonly occurs in which of the following?
Neurogenic shock is characterized by which of the following?
A child presents with bowing of legs, delayed walking, and widening of wrists. There is a history of poor nutrition. What is the most likely diagnosis?
During surgery, a surgeon accidentally touches a non-sterile surface with a sterile glove. What is the most appropriate immediate action?
A 40-year-old man presents with pain over the lateral aspect of the elbow, aggravated by wrist extension against resistance. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A 30-year-old woman presents with pain all over the radial side of the wrist, especially when lifting her baby. The Finkelstein test is positive. What is the diagnosis?
A 65-year-old woman presents with back pain and bilateral leg pain while walking, which is relieved by sitting and bending forward. What is the most likely diagnosis?

An office worker develops chronic back pain after years of improper sitting posture and poorly designed workstation equipment. The occupational physician recommends redesigning the chair and workstation to fit the worker. Which occupational health principle is being applied?

A 40-year-old textile worker complains of chest tightness and breathlessness after several years of working in a carbon processing factory. Examinations show features of occupational lung disease related to dust exposure. Which condition is most likely?

A miner presents with progressive dyspnea and chronic cough after long-term exposure to rock dust while drilling and crushing stones and rocks in a quarry. Which occupational lung disease is most strongly associated with this exposure?

A factory worker has been exposed to continuous machine noise for several years. Workplace measurements show sound levels above the limit requiring monitoring according to the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) standards. What is the threshold noise level for an 8-hour time-weighted average exposure?

A farmer develops a fever and muscle spasms after stepping on a contaminated nail while working in the soil. Infection due to occupational exposure is suspected. Which occupational hazard category best explains this condition?

A construction worker spends long hours working under intense sunlight. After several years, he developed progressive painless loss of vision. Examination reveals lens opacity with preserved pupillary reflex. Which occupational disease is most likely responsible?
After heavy rainfall, a city reports increased cases of gastroenteritis. What is the most likely source of water pollution?
Farmers use excessive fertilizers. Nearby water bodies show an algal bloom, which causes an increase in biological demand. Which pollutant is responsible for this issue?

A public health survey in an urban slum reveals overcrowding, poor ventilation, and damp housing conditions. Many residents report frequent respiratory infections. Which housing factor most strongly contributes to this problem?
A 60-year-old coal miner presents with progressive breathlessness, and chest X-ray reveals nodular lung fibrosis. Which occupational lung disease is most likely?

In a rural village, many households cook using biomass fuels such as wood and animal dung. Recent reports suggest increased levels of indoor pollution. Which public health intervention would most effectively reduce indoor air pollution?

An 8-year-old child living near a busy industrial area presents with a persistent cough and reduced lung function. Environmental monitoring shows high levels of airborne pollutants. Which of the following pollutants is most strongly associated with respiratory diseases in children?

A 48-year-old construction worker presents with chronic lower back pain for the past 6 months. His job involves repeatedly carrying heavy cement bags without mechanical assistance. Workplace inspection reveals improper lifting techniques. Which intervention would most effectively prevent this musculoskeletal disorder?

answers.option: Ergonomic workplace redesign with mechanical lifting aids
Health education on back pain management

question: During a high-smog period in Lahore, the provincial health department reports an Air Quality Index (AQI) of 350. Simultaneously, local emergency departments report a 40% increase in pediatric patients presenting with acute respiratory distress, wheezing, and inflamed lung linings. What is the most appropriate immediate public health recommendation for the general population based on this AQI level?

answers.option: Issue an alert to avoid outdoor exertion by all residents
Limit use of plastic shopping bags

question: A rural district hit by heavy monsoon flooding reports a sharp rise in watery diarrhea among young children. Public health teams observe that the local water sources are submerged, and open defecation has become prevalent due to destroyed infrastructure. According to UNICEF's emergency WASH strategy, which immediate action is the most effective for reducing child morbidity?

answers.option: Initiating a mass vaccination campaign for Hepatitis A
Rapid setup of communal latrines and providing point-of-use water treatment
Constructing a permanent centralized sewage system
Conducting long-term environmental impact assessments of the flood
Distributing high-energy protein supplements to all affected children

question: A 38-year-old man came for periodical examination to an occupational clinic working in an iron foundry as a welder, where inhalation of iron oxide fumes or dust is common and affecting workers. Which occupational lung disease is most likely this worker can suffer?

A 32-year-old female schizophrenic patient is brought to the ER with complaints of nausea, vomiting and right upper quadrant pain. Lab monitoring showed deranged liver function tests. Her urinary drug screening showed acetaminophen positive. She is diagnosed with a case of acetaminophen poisoning. Which of the following agents can be used as an antidote in this patient?

↑A 27-year-old female presented to the OPD with a history of pain and swelling of joints of both hands for the last two years. She has noticed a change in the shape of her right thumb for the last two months. She has been taking different painkillers with minimal relief from pain over the past two years. Which of the following drugs should be added to her treatment?

A 14-year-old boy was brought to an orthopedic clinic with complaints of fever, chills and
malaise. On physical examination, a swelling was noticed in front of his right leg, and
Brodie's abscess was found on x-ray examination. His father had a history of the same leg
injury after falling 2 months back while playing football. On physical examination, there was a limp without pain. What is the most probable diagnosis in this patient?

During a biopsy of a bone tissue, the pathologist found osteoblastic and phase predominant over osteoclastic. There was a jigsaw puzzle appearance with a mosaic
pattern. The genetic workup showed the mutation of the SQSTM1 gene. The patient was 35
years old male and history of repeated fractures and enlargement of the craniofacial skeleton was provided. What is the most probable diagnosis in this patient?
During the repair sequences of fractured bone, osteoprogenitor cells are stimulated to form osteoblasts and osteoclasts. Which cells are responsible for activating the osteoprogenitor cells?

A 6-year-old female child presented with short stature, malformed bones and chest wall
abnormalities. Patient had gross abnormalities of hyaline cartilage, affecting growth
plates, costal cartilages and articular surfaces. Pediatrician is suspecting an underlying
enzyme deficiency. What is the most likely diagnosis in this case?

A 5-year-old boy had a fragile skeleton with a history of repeated fractures. He had short
stature, clinical examination revealed growth retardation, blue sclera, teeth abnormalities
and impaired hearing. His older sister also had similar complaints. He was a product of
consanguineous marriage. These abnormalities are caused by a defect in which of the following?

A 40-year-old man presented with painful foot swelling. Biopsy showed skin covered
fibrocollagenous tissue with tan-white, chalky deposits. Histology showed nodular
aggregates consisting of acellular, amorphous, pale eosinophilic material surrounded by
a palisading arrangement of histiocytes and multinucleated giant cells. The material showed needle-like crystals. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A 30-year-old male presents with a gunshot injury to the femur. X-ray shows a highly comminuted fracture with multiple bone fragments. Which type of firearm injury is most likely responsible?
A patient with a gunshot wound to the leg presents with absent distal pulses and severe pain. What is the most appropriate next step?

answers.option: Immediate vascular assessment and surgical exploration

question: A patient with chronic osteomyelitis undergoes an X-ray. Which of the following findings is most characteristic?
A patient with chronic osteomyelitis of the tibia has a sequestrum seen on imaging. What is the definitive treatment?

A 70-year-old woman presents with the sudden onset of back pain after minimal trauma. X-ray shows a wedge compression fracture of the vertebra. What is the most likely underlying
condition?
Which of the following fractures is most commonly associated with osteoporosis in elderly patients?
What is the term used for bony outgrowths usually seen at the periphery of osteoarthritic joints?

A 50-year-old woman presents with a 6-month history of joint pain, swelling, and morning stiffness lasting more than 1 hour. Examination shows symmetrical swelling of the metacarpophalangeal and proximal interphalangeal joints. Rheumatoid factor is positive. A synovial biopsy is performed. Which of the following is the most characteristic
histologic finding?
A patient presents with wrist drop following a fracture of the midshaft of the humerus. Which nerve is most likely injured?
Which NSAID is most likely to cause irreversible inhibition of cyclooxygenase?

A 12-year-old obese boy presents with a 4-month history of progressive limping and intermittent pain in the left knee. There is no history of trauma. On examination, the left lower limb is externally rotated, and there is painful restriction of internal rotation of the hip. What is the most likely diagnosis?

On routine neonatal examination, a 1-day-old boy is found to have a dimple at the lumbosacral region, 3 cm away from the anal verge. The base of the dimple is not clearly visualised. The child is otherwise active, and neurological examination is unremarkable. What is the best intervention in the management of this child?

answers.option: Refer to neurosurgery for surgical intervention
Watchful waiting till the child is 6 months of age
Reassure parents and no further evaluation is required

question:
A 9-year-old boy is brought for evaluation of short stature. Previous assessments show that his height has consistently been tracked along the 3rd percentile, but his growth
velocity remains normal. His weight is appropriate for his height. On examination, he has no
dysmorphosis. His height is 124cm (at the 3rd percentile), and the upper segment/lower segment ratio is normal for age. Systemic examination is unremarkable. Tanner staging is prepubertal. His bone age corresponds to his chronological age. What is the most likely
cause of short stature in this child?

A 6-year-old boy is brought in for concerns regarding height development. Mother
noticed that the child has always been short among his classmates and his peers. He
has no history of any chronic illness. Nutritional history is adequate. His height is 100cm
and weight is 19kg. The upper-to-lower segment ratio is normal for his age. His
father's height is 155cm, and his mother's height is 150cm. What is the mid-parental height
for this child?

A newborn is brought to the OPD for well-baby assessment. He was born at 38 weeks of gestation with a C-section due to transverse lie. Baby is vitally stable. On head-to-toe examination, the right foot is found to be plantar flexed at the ankle joint and inverted. What is the 1st line of treatment?

A 5-year-old child is brought to OPD for assessment of a limp in the right leg for the past two months. He has no history of trauma or fever. Initially, it was painless, but for the last week, the child started to feel pain while walking. Pain is localized to the right groin. months. Bone scan reveals an avascular femoral head. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 72-year-old retired teacher is brought in by his son due to increasing difficulty in
handling finances and solving day-to-day problems. He is able to recall past events
clearly but struggles with new tasks and complex decision-making. His speech and
vocabulary remain intact. What is the most likely explanation for this presentation?

An 80-year-old widower presents with irritability, fear of death, and a persistent feeling
that his life has been meaningless. He frequently expresses regret and believes he has
wasted his life. According to Erikson's psychosocial theory, this patient is most likely
experiencing which of the following?

During repeated stimulation of skeletal muscle, a pharmacologic agent selectively inhibits SERCA pumps in the sarcoplasmic reticulum. Despite cessation of neural stimulation, muscle fibres fail to relax promptly. Which is the primary intracellular event responsible for this impaired relaxation?

A 54-year-old male presents with sudden-onset, excruciating pain and swelling in his right big toe that began overnight. Prior history of a similar episode three months ago after a seafood dinner. On examination, the joint is erythematous, warm, and exquisitely tender. Arthrocentesis is performed. Which of the following findings on synovial fluid analysis is most diagnostic for this patient's condition?

answers.option: WBC count > 50,000/mm³ with > 75% neutrophils and no crystals
Needle-shaped crystals with strong negative birefringence
Rhomboid-shaped crystals with weak positive birefringence
Small, circular crystals with a "Maltese cross" appearance

question: A 45-year-old obese male with a known case of hypertension presents to the emergency department with a history of sudden excruciating pain in the right knee joint for the last 1 day, with no fever or any other joint symptoms. His urate level is 9.2mg/dl, CRP 34mg/di(N=10), and Creatinine is 0.9mg/dl. What is the appropriate treatment to initiate?

A 26-year-old female presents to OPD with a 3-month history of symmetric joint pain involving the small joints of her hands and wrists. She also reports significant fatigue and a facial rash that worsens with sun exposure. On examination, there is non-erosive arthritis and a fixed erythema over the malar eminences, sparing the nasolabial folds. Lab Report shows a positive ANA (1:1280, speckled pattern) and mild leukopenia and thrombocytopenia. Which of the following is the most specific lab marker to confirm the diagnosis of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE)?

A 30-year-old woman with a known diagnosis of SLE presents for a follow-up. She is currently taking Hydroxychloroquine, but she is still having joint pains with stiffness requiring daily painkillers. Her liver and kidney functions are normal. In addition to low-dose corticosteroids, which of the following is the most appropriate therapy to add for this patient?

A 27-year-old man presents with a 6-month history of lower back pain and morning stiffness lasting more than 1 hour. The pain improves with exercise but not with rest. He also reports heel pain, especially when walking. On examination, there is tenderness at the Achilles tendon insertion site. Laboratory tests reveal a negative rheumatoid factor. Which of the following is the most characteristic feature of the condition affecting this patient?

answers.option: Isolated involvement of the temporomandibular joint
Symmetric small joint involvement of the hands

question: A 26-year-old male presents with 4 months history of back pain and morning stiffness of 2 hours. The pain improves with mobility and worsens during periods of inactivity. He also complains of bilateral heel pain. Examination reveals bilateral sacral tenderness and plantar fasciitis. Which of the following extra-articular features is consistent with seronegative inflammatory arthritis?
